title: Direct identification via explicit identifiers in registration data
description: The parent registration flow includes explicit identifiers such as email, name, and government ID. When Authentication Service receives and processes this flow, the data subject can be directly identified from the transmitted data.
assumptions: Government ID, email, and name are genuine user attributes and are handled by the Authentication Service as part of account registration.

title: Disclosure of highly sensitive registration attributes in transit to the service
description: The flow carries confidential personal data, including password and government ID, from the parent user to the Authentication Service. If the transmission channel or receiving endpoint is insufficiently protected, these attributes could be exposed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: This threat concerns the data flow and receiving process handling; transport or endpoint protections are not guaranteed by the DFD alone.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node selected by best judgement; the retrieved context did not provide a disclosure-specific node citation for this exact case.

title: Collection of potentially unnecessary personal data during registration
description: The registration flow includes government ID and name in addition to email, password, and a six-digit code. If these attributes are not strictly necessary for authentication or account creation, the Authentication Service may be collecting more personal data than needed, conflicting with data minimization and purpose limitation.
assumptions: Government ID may not be necessary for basic authentication; necessity depends on the service's regulatory and business context.
uncertainty_note: The exact non-compliance node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include a non-compliance tree citation.

title: Excessive storage of parent account personal data
description: The authentication service stores a parent account in the users collection. If the stored record contains more personal data than strictly necessary for authentication and account management, the write operation creates an avoidable disclosure risk because unnecessary personal data is persisted in the datastore.
assumptions: Assumes the parent account record may include profile, contact, or relationship attributes beyond what is needed for authentication/account provisioning.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data disclosure/minimality guidance; exact node label may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Stored parent account enables identification of the parent
description: Writing the parent account to the users collection likely stores direct or indirectly identifying attributes. Once persisted, the datastore contents can identify a natural person, especially if usernames, email addresses, phone numbers, or stable account identifiers are retained.
assumptions: Assumes the parent account contains direct identifiers or a unique persistent account identifier.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node may differ by LINDDUN Pro version; applicability is high because account records are typically identifying.

title: Parent account record may be linkable across contexts
description: Persisting a parent account in a central users collection can allow the same individual to be linked across sessions, services, or family-related records via a stable account identifier. This can enable correlation of activities and relationships that were not meant to be associated.
assumptions: Assumes the users collection uses a persistent key reused across multiple features or datasets.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; exact node id may vary.

title: Parent account storage may exceed consent or expected purpose
description: Storing the parent account in the users collection may be non-compliant if the purpose, legal basis, retention, or scope of stored personal data was not clearly communicated or agreed to. The privacy risk arises at storage because persisted data can be reused beyond the user's reasonable expectations.
assumptions: Assumes there may be insufficient notice, consent, or purpose limitation for all attributes written to the collection.
uncertainty_note: This depends on organizational/legal context not visible in the DFD; included because compliance risks often attach to account-data storage.

title: JWT and user data may disclose excessive personal information to the parent
description: The flow sends a JWT together with user data from the Authentication Service to the Parent User. If the JWT contains embedded claims beyond what is strictly necessary, or if the accompanying user data includes unnecessary profile attributes, sensitive or identifying information may be exposed to the recipient or to anyone who can observe the message at the endpoint.

uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; retrieved context confirms Information Disclosure applies to Process->ExternalEntity flows but does not provide the exact I-tree node citation.

description: A stable JWT subject, account identifiers, roles, device-related claims, or correlated user attributes in the response can allow the parent to link sessions and build a profile of the individual over time. Combining token claims with returned user data may make different interactions attributable to the same person or household.
assumptions: Assumes the token or returned data contains stable identifiers or recurring attributes across sessions.
uncertainty_note: L.2.2.1 is supported by retrieved context for profiling an individual; applicability depends on the actual claims and attributes present in the JWT and payload.

This is a privacy threat if the response includes attributes not necessary for authentication, or if child-related data is shared without a clear legal basis or compatible purpose.

If the service collects, stores, or exposes this information more broadly than necessary, the flow causes unnecessary disclosure of both the parent's identity and the child-parent relationship.

title: Streaming to a child may violate child-privacy, minimization, or lawful-basis requirements
description: Because the recipient is a child user, this flow may trigger heightened compliance obligations. If the service streams personalized content or collects excessive playback telemetry without appropriate parental authorization, age-appropriate notices, retention limits, or a valid lawful basis, the processing associated with the stream could be non-compliant with child privacy requirements and data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the system processes personal data about a child and applicable law or policy imposes enhanced protections for children.
uncertainty_note: Compliance obligations depend on jurisdiction and implementation details; this is a genuine risk but legal applicability is context-dependent.

title: Excessive disclosure of child browsing data to the AI engine
description: The planned flow sends child browsing data from the childprofiles collection to the AI Recommendation Engine. If the full browsing history or rich behavioral attributes are transferred when only a subset is needed for recommendations, the flow creates avoidable disclosure of children's personal data within the system, violating data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes the AI engine can operate on fewer, aggregated, or pseudonymized features than the raw browsing dataset currently envisaged for transfer.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgment based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimization patterns; the retrieved context confirms Dd applies to DataStore->Process flows but does not provide the exact subtree.

title: Inference of sensitive child traits from browsing data
description: Browsing data can enable the AI Recommendation Engine to infer additional personal or sensitive attributes about a child, such as interests, vulnerabilities, developmental stage, health concerns, or family circumstances, beyond what was originally stored or expected. This creates an inference threat on this flow because the transferred data supports derivation of new privacy-relevant knowledge.
assumptions: Assumes recommendation models use behavioral patterns in a way that can derive latent attributes rather than only producing non-personal aggregate outputs.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree node id is approximate; retrieved context establishes inference as applicable to DataStore->Process but does not include subtree details.

title: Use of child browsing data for recommendations may be incompatible with the original collection purpose
description: The flow is marked as planned and repurposes child browsing data from the childprofiles collection for an AI Recommendation Engine. If the browsing data was originally collected for account operation, safety, or history tracking rather than AI personalization, this new processing purpose may be insufficiently transparent or incompatible with the original purpose, leaving the child or guardian unaware of how the data is used.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation and transparency for AI personalization have not yet been fully specified or communicated.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgment; context only indicates Unawareness is applicable for DataStore->Process flows.

title: Potential non-compliance from processing children's browsing data without an appropriate legal basis or child-specific safeguards
description: Sending child browsing data to an AI Recommendation Engine may trigger heightened compliance obligations because the data concerns children and supports profiling/personalization. If this planned processing lacks a clear legal basis, age-appropriate notices, parental authorization where required, retention limits, or profiling safeguards, the flow creates a non-compliance threat.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to privacy obligations that impose special protections for children's data and profiling activities.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate; the compliance concern is well-grounded, but the retrieved context does not provide the specific Nc subtree.

title: Unnecessary disclosure of browsing data to third-party advertisers
description: The planned flow sends browsing data from the AI Recommendation Engine to third-party advertisers. Browsing data is personal data and sharing it with advertisers is likely not strictly necessary for providing recommendations, creating an avoidable explicit disclosure to a third party that violates data minimization and purpose limitation.
assumptions: Assumes the browsing data can relate to identifiable or singlable users/devices and that advertisers are separate third parties rather than processors acting solely on documented instructions.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selection is based on best judgement for explicit third-party disclosure/minimization; the retrieved context confirms Dd applies to Process->ExternalEntity flows but does not provide the exact subtree text.

title: Cross-context identification of users by advertisers
description: Sharing browsing data with advertisers can enable them to identify, single out, or map the same user/device across multiple services, especially when combined with existing ad-tech identifiers, IP addresses, fingerprints, or account data already held by the advertiser.
assumptions: Assumes the shared browsing data includes stable identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or rich event patterns that can be linked with advertiser-held records.
uncertainty_note: Applicable because Process->ExternalEntity flows can carry identifiability risk, but the exact presence of identifiers in this planned flow is not stated.

title: Linkability of browsing behavior across services and datasets
description: The disclosure of browsing data to third-party advertisers may allow those advertisers to link events from this system with data from other websites, apps, or campaigns, constructing broader behavioral profiles about the same person or device.
assumptions: Assumes advertisers receive enough attributes, timestamps, device metadata, or campaign identifiers to correlate records across contexts.
uncertainty_note: The exact subtree id is chosen by best judgement for linkability via shared attributes; the flow description strongly suggests this risk even if exact fields are unspecified.

title: Detectability of user activity by third-party advertisers
description: Sending browsing data to advertisers makes the user's visits, interactions, or interest in certain content detectable by those third parties. Even if the data is partially pseudonymized, the transmission itself can reveal that a particular user/device engaged with the service at a given time.
assumptions: Assumes the advertiser can observe receipt timing, network metadata, or event payloads tied to a browser/app instance.
uncertainty_note: Detectability is a genuine risk on this outbound flow, though the exact degree depends on implementation details and whether data is batched or real-time.

title: Sharing browsing data with advertisers without valid user consent or compatible purpose
description: The planned disclosure to third-party advertisers may be incompatible with the original purpose for which browsing data was collected, or may occur without freely given, specific, informed, and revocable consent where such consent is required. This creates a non-compliance risk under privacy and data-protection obligations.
assumptions: Assumes browsing data was initially collected for service use or recommendations rather than advertising disclosure, and that applicable law or policy requires consent or another valid legal basis for such third-party sharing.
uncertainty_note: This is a strong compliance concern for advertising disclosures, but the actual legal basis, notices, contracts, and jurisdiction are not provided.

title: Stored government ID images directly identify individuals
description: The file system stores images of government-issued identity documents. These images contain explicit identifiers and often photos, document numbers, names, and dates of birth, so merely storing them in DS4 creates a strong identifying privacy threat if accessed, indexed, or reused beyond the intended verification purpose.
assumptions: Government ID images include directly identifying content and are retained in readable form in backend/uploads/.

title: Government ID images may disclose more personal data than necessary
description: A full government ID image typically contains multiple sensitive attributes beyond what may be needed for authentication or age/identity verification, such as full legal name, document number, date of birth, nationality, address, photo, and signature. Storing the full image in the file system risks disclosure of excessive personal information if the data is accessed, reused, or insufficiently minimized.
assumptions: The whole ID image is stored rather than extracting and retaining only the minimum required attributes.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; the retrieved context did not include a disclosure subtree citation for this specific case.

title: Users may be unaware that raw ID images are stored in backend uploads
description: If the system stores raw government ID images in a backend file store without clear notice, users may not understand that highly sensitive identity documents are retained, for how long, and for which secondary operational purposes. This creates an unawareness threat around storage and retention of sensitive identity data.
assumptions: Notice and consent/just-in-time explanation about raw ID-image storage and retention may be limited or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Exact U subtree node may vary depending on the project’s threat tree version; U.1 is used as best judgement.

title: Storing full ID images may violate data minimization or retention obligations
description: Persisting government ID images in a general file-system uploads area may be unnecessary or excessive relative to the authentication purpose, especially if the images are retained longer than needed for verification. This can create non-compliance risk with privacy obligations such as purpose limitation, storage limitation, and data minimization.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements restrict collection and retention of identity-document images to what is necessary and proportionate.
uncertainty_note: Exact Nc subtree citation is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include the non-compliance subtree.

title: Insufficient evidence of who stored or modified ID images may enable repudiation
description: If uploads to backend/uploads/ are not accompanied by reliable audit records, the authentication service or operators may later be unable to prove which government ID image was stored, replaced, or deleted, and by whom or on whose behalf. This weakens accountability for handling sensitive identity evidence.
assumptions: Audit logging, integrity protection, and tamper-evident records for file writes may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Threat applicability depends on actual audit and integrity controls; included because repudiation at storage is a plausible privacy/accountability issue for this flow.

title: JWT in localStorage can identify the user/device
description: Storing a JWT in browser localStorage creates a persistent client-side identifier. If the token contains user claims or a stable subject identifier, scripts running in the origin can read it and use it to identify the user or browser instance across sessions and interactions.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains stable identifying claims (for example sub, email, account id) or otherwise uniquely maps to a user/session, and that localStorage is readable by application scripts.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on generic LINDDUN Pro identification threats; exact sub-node naming may vary by threat-tree version.

title: JWT in localStorage enables linkability across visits and app actions
description: A JWT stored in localStorage can act as a stable linkable token, allowing separate browser sessions, page views, or in-app actions to be correlated to the same user or device. This can enable profiling beyond what is necessary for the immediate authentication transaction.
assumptions: Assumes the same token or a token carrying a stable subject is reused across multiple requests, views, or time periods.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node id may differ by version; threat applicability is strong even if the specific node label is approximate.

title: JWT contents in localStorage may disclose personal data to scripts or local device users
description: If the JWT is a readable bearer token containing claims such as user id, email, role, tenant, or other attributes, storing it in localStorage exposes those contents to any script executing in the origin and potentially to others with access to the browser profile on the device. This creates confidentiality and privacy disclosure risk.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is not encrypted at rest in the browser and contains privacy-relevant claims rather than being an opaque reference only.
uncertainty_note: Applies most strongly to self-contained JWTs with readable claims; if the token is opaque and short-lived, disclosure impact is lower.

title: Persisting JWT in localStorage may exceed user expectations or consent
description: Users may not reasonably expect an authentication token to be persisted in browser localStorage, potentially surviving browser restarts and remaining accessible to application scripts. If this persistence is not clearly communicated or justified, the storage practice may violate data minimization, storage limitation, or consent/choice expectations.
assumptions: Assumes the application does not clearly inform users about token persistence duration and purpose, or lacks an alternative less persistent mechanism.
uncertainty_note: This is context-dependent: whether it is a true non-compliance issue depends on the system's notices, legal basis, retention controls, and jurisdiction.

title: Excessive profile linking in child history returned to parent
description: The child history sent from Child Profile Management to the parent may aggregate multiple events, contexts, or data categories into a single view, enabling stronger profiling of the child than necessary for the review purpose. Combining education, behavior, health, location, or usage history in one response can reveal additional inferences about the child.
assumptions: The returned history may contain multiple categories of records over time rather than a narrowly scoped summary.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for linking-by-aggregation; exact node naming may vary across LINDDUN Pro catalogs.

title: Identifiable child records disclosed to parent beyond necessary scope
description: The flow returns child history for parent review, which likely contains directly identifying or highly specific historical records tied to a particular child. If the response includes more granular identifiers or event details than needed, the child becomes unnecessarily identifiable within the transaction and any downstream handling by the parent.
assumptions: The history payload contains child-specific records and may include timestamps, unique identifiers, or detailed event narratives.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine identifiability risk if minimization is weak; exact node id may differ in a project-specific threat tree.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child history to the wrong parent or household member
description: A confidentiality failure on this outbound flow could expose the child's history to an unintended recipient, such as the wrong parent account, another guardian, or someone using a shared device/session. Because historical records can be sensitive, misdelivery or overbroad access on this flow constitutes a significant disclosure threat.
assumptions: Parent access control, session binding, or recipient verification may be imperfect, or the parent device/account may be shared.
uncertainty_note: High confidence in the threat, but the precise tree node id is approximate.

title: Overly detailed history reveals sensitive patterns about the child
description: Even when sent to an authorized parent, the history may contain excessive detail such as precise timestamps, longitudinal patterns, special-category information, or contextual notes that make the child highly detectable or expose sensitive habits and conditions. The issue is not only disclosure to outsiders, but the granularity of data made observable through the flow.
assumptions: The returned history includes detailed chronological or contextual records rather than a minimized summary.
uncertainty_note: Node id chosen by best fit for detectability/excessive observability; exact catalog wording may vary.

title: Parent may be unaware of the extent of child-history processing and sharing
description: The flow assumes the parent is presented with the child's history, but the child and possibly the parent may not understand what categories of history are retrieved, from which sources, for what period, and under what access rules. If the retrieval occurs without clear notice, the data subject lacks awareness of processing and disclosure.
assumptions: Transparency information is not clearly presented at the point of review.
uncertainty_note: Applies if the UI/API does not explain the history scope and sources; exact tree node id may differ.

title: Child-history sharing may exceed consent or parental-authority boundaries
description: Returning child history to a parent may be non-compliant if the system lacks a valid legal basis, fails to respect custody/guardianship constraints, or shares records outside the consented purpose and retention scope. Special caution is needed where the child's age, evolving capacity, or separated parental rights affect who may view history.
assumptions: Access rights can vary by guardian status, child age, jurisdiction, and category of history data.
uncertainty_note: High confidence in the compliance risk; the exact tree-node id is approximate because the retrieved context did not include the detailed compliance tree.
